question.problem:
Find the values of the constants $a$ and $b$ that make the function $g(x)$ below continuous at $x=-2$ and $x=0.$

$$
g(x)=\{\begin{aligned}-x, & x\le -2 \\ a{x}^{2}+b, & -2<x<0 \\ 6, & x\ge 0\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
At $x=-2,$ the left-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (-2)^{-}}g(x) & =g(-2) \\  & =-(-2) \\  & =2,\end{aligned}
$$

and the right-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (-2)^{+}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to (-2)^{+}}(a{x}^{2}+b) \\  & =a(-2)^{2}+b \\  & =4a+b.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $g(x)$ to be continuous at $x=-2,$ we require that

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (-2)^{-}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to (-2)^{+}}g(x) \\ 2 & =4a+b\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, at $x=0,$ the left-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}(a{x}^{2}+b) \\  & =a(0)^{2}+b \\  & =0+b \\  & =b,\end{aligned}
$$

and the right-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}g(x) & =g(0) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $g(x)$ to be continuous at $x=0,$ we require that

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}g(x) \\ b & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's solve the following system of equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4a+b=2 \\ b=6.\end{aligned}
$$

We can replace $b$ by $6$ in the first equation. Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4a+b & =2 \\ 4a+6 & =2 \\ 4a & =-4 \\ a & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)$ is continuous at $x=-2$ and $x=0$ for $a=-1$ and $b=6.$
